extracted.intended_audience: employers, human resources professionals, labor attorneys, policy stakeholders, and rulemaking commenters interested in FLSA EAP exemption salary/HCE thresholds
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and methodological criteria the Department of Labor used to set, update, and analyze the standard salary level and the highly compensated employee (HCE) total annual compensation threshold for the EAP overtime exemption, including data sources, adjustment methods, timing, and regulatory-process decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating mechanism for salary level and HCE threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule establishes an updating mechanism pursuant to which the standard salary level and HCE total annual compensation threshold will be regularly updated (triennially).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial updates use pooled data for recent 3 years (2021–2023) adjusted to reflect 2023; initial update dates and applicability described (initial updates applicable July 1, 2024; new standard salary level and HCE requirement applicable January 1, 2025). The Department states the RFA and Executive Order 13563 do not require notice-and-comment rulemaking to precede future triennial updates and includes estimates of future costs of updates in the final rule and NPRM (see sections VII and VIII).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard salary level set to 35th percentile in lowest-wage Census Region
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard salary level is increased to the 35th percentile of weekly earnings of full-time salaried employees in the lowest-wage Census Region (the South).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach is intended to restore the salary level's historic screening function and account for low-wage industries and regions by using earnings data from the lowest-wage Census Region to set the salary level.

rubrics_metrics.name: HCE total annual compensation threshold increase and severability
rubrics_metrics.description: The increase in the HCE total annual compensation threshold is intended to be independent of, and severable from, the increase in the standard salary level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The HCE threshold will also be regularly updated under the updating provision. Department provides example numeric values for scenarios depending on whether initial updates go into effect (e.g., $132,964 vs $107,432 under certain circumstances).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data source for percentile calculations (CPS MORG nonhourly earnings)
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining earnings percentiles the Department looked at nonhourly earnings for full-time workers from the CPS MORG data collected by BLS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BLS publishes quarterly and annual percentile earnings estimates beginning with 2022 data at the cited URL; the Department treats nonhourly workers' earnings as an appropriate proxy for salaried workers (uses same approach as 2004, 2016, 2019 rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of pooled 3-year data and adjustment to reflect current year
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department used pooled data for the most recent 3 years (2021, 2022, 2023), adjusting them to reflect 2023, for the initial updates to both the standard salary level and HCE total annual compensation threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM had considered using 2022 data as an alternative; the final rule uses pooled 3-year data per prior practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment method for pooled observations (CPI-U)
rubrics_metrics.description: Previous rulemakings adjusted salaries in the pooled data using the CPI-U; the Department decided to continue adjusting observations using CPI-U despite mixed wage/inflation relationships during 2021–2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department recognizes pandemic-era disruptions and mixed effects but continues prior practice of CPI-U adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling with Department probability codes in economic analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department's economic modeling is done using the Department's probability codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See section VII and prior rules; modeling and impact estimation reference these probability codes and associated methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'affected workers'
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'affected workers' refers to the population of potentially affected EAP workers who either pass the standard duties test and earn at least $684 but less than the new salary level of $1,128 per week or pass only the HCE duties test and earn at least $107,432 but less than the new HCE compensation level of $151,164 per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition is used in the Department's impact and population analyses; estimates excluding named occupations are characterized as conservative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of named occupations and non-EAP exemptions from impact counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimates of affected workers exclude workers in named occupations (e.g., teachers, attorneys, physicians) and those exempt under another non-EAP overtime exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluding these 8.1 million 'named occupations' makes estimates conservative; including them increases the share whose exemption status depends on duties rather than salary to 76 percent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary-basis criteria parity between standard exemption and HCE test
rubrics_metrics.description: The criteria for determining if an employee is paid on a 'salary basis' are identical under the standard exemption criteria and the HCE test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Helix Energy Solutions, 143 S. Ct. at 683; however, §541.601(b)(1) does not permit employers to use nondiscretionary bonuses, incentives, and commissions to satisfy the weekly standard salary level requirement for HCE workers (unlike the standard salary where up to 10% may be used).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of nondiscretionary bonuses/incentives for standard salary vs HCE
rubrics_metrics.description: §541.602(a)(3) allows employers to use nondiscretionary bonuses, incentives, and commissions to satisfy up to 10 percent of the weekly standard salary level when applying the standard salary and duties tests, but §541.601(b)(1) does not permit such payments to satisfy the weekly standard salary level requirement for HCE workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This difference affects how employers may count compensation toward meeting salary thresholds for the two tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary level as screening device; duties test retained
rubrics_metrics.description: The salary level test serves as a screening test to screen obviously nonexempt employees from the exemption, but the Department preserves a primary role for examination of duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department cites Stein Report and prior rulemaking history; large numbers of salaried workers above the salary level will nonetheless not meet duties test and remain nonexempt, underscoring importance of duties analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of long test methodology to calculate long test salary level (10th percentile)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department calculated the value of the long test salary level using the 10th percentile of earnings of likely exempt workers in low-wage industries and regions, consistent with the long test methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department notes minor historical variations do not deprive the methodology of usefulness in determining an appropriate salary level now.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single nationwide salary level (no multiple regional/industry/small-business levels)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines requests to adopt multiple salary level tests for different regions, industries, and/or small businesses, instead maintaining a single salary level that applies nationwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with longstanding practice and prior final rules; cited commenters who suggested multiple levels but Department rejects them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice to avoid inflation-indexing for replicating long test (reject Oxford Economics approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines the suggestion to replicate the long test by updating the 1975 long test level solely for inflation, which would conflict with historical practice of avoiding inflation indicators in updating the salary level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explained in section V.B; Department prefers percentile- and earnings-based methodologies over simple inflation adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting for workers with zero earnings/hours in reweighting/data cleaning
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department reweighted for workers reporting zero earnings, and eliminated without reweighting workers who reported both usually working zero hours and working zero hours in the past week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justified because demographic and employment characteristics are similar across included/excluded populations; acknowledges potential under/overestimation effects depending on overtime patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and rounding conventions for analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers are reported at varying levels of aggregation and are generally rounded to a single decimal point, but calculations are performed using exact numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some reported totals or calculations may not match due to rounding of components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic analysis discount rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise specified, annualized values will be presented using the 7 percent real discount rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used throughout the Department's regulatory impact analysis for annualizing values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and phase-in considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the Department's approach is not a phase-in, the effect of increasing the salary level twice in 8 months resembles a multi-step implementation; the Department adjusted applicability dates to provide employers time to adjust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial updates applicable July 1, 2024; full new standards applicable January 1, 2025. Department considered commenters' requests for phasing but treated the approach as not a formal phase-in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of O*NET and occupation descriptors as reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The O*NET database contains hundreds of standardized and occupation-specific descriptors and is cited as a resource.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: O*NET referenced for occupation descriptors that may inform duties analyses and classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservative estimation principle in population impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department characterizes certain analytical choices (e.g., excluding named occupations) as conservative, intending to avoid overstating the number of affected workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion notes that including excluded occupations would increase the percentage for whom duties determine exemption status, and that conservative choices tend to understate transfer payments/costs in some directions.
